    The year climate term of an ignition or an escape fit

    fitYearClimate.Rd

    Fits E[O_y] = P_y * exp(beta * z_y) / norm, beta >= 0, where P_y and O_y are the out-of-year predicted and observed ignitions (or escapes) of year y (yearTotals) and z_y is the standardised yearly mean of variable (fireSenseUtils::yearClimateMeans() of the raw covariates, the unweighted mean over the rows with the variable and with core (coreFraction above 0): centre is the mean over the fit years of the yearly means, scale their sd). beta is the coefficient of glm(observed ~ 0 + z, offset = log(scaleToObservedLevel(observed, predicted)), family = poisson), floored at 0: the offset removes the overall level gap, as fireSenseUtils::yearEffectSD() does, so beta is only the year-to-year response. norm is the mean of exp(beta * z_y) over the fit years, so the multiplier averages 1 over them. beta is 0 (with a message) if there are fewer than 2 years with a mean, the means do not vary, nothing is observed or expected, or the glm fails; center and scale are always finite.

    fitYearClimate(
  variable,
  raw,
  yearTotals,
  shape = "loglinear",
  weights = "equal"
)

    Arguments

    variable

    Covariate name, with or without underscores. The column must be in raw.

    raw

    The raw ignition covariates, sim$fireSense_ignitionCovariates.

    yearTotals

    The data.frame of outOfFoldYearTotals(): year (calendar year; the fit's is standardised when rescaleVars, so map it with calendarYearOf() first), observed, predicted; or NULL.

    shape

    "loglinear" (exp(beta * z), the default) or "logistic".

    weights

    "equal" (every year counts the same) or "climate" (fireSenseUtils::annualYearWeights()).

    Value

    list(variable, center, scale, beta, norm), or with shape = "logistic" list(variable, center, scale, shape, k, ratio, norm, bounds); then weights when not "equal". variable is the covariate's column name.

    Details

    With shape = "logistic" the term is an S-curve through its midpoint at z = 0, the ELF's average year: g(z) = 1 + (ratio - 1) * plogis(k * z) divided by norm, the mean of g over the fit years (so it averages 1, as above). Two parameters are fitted, k >= 0 (the steepness, in 1 / sd) and ratio >= 1 (the upper level over the floor); the floor is 1 before norm, so the multiplier is always positive, and it saturates beyond the fit range at ratio / norm (the dry side, z > 0) and 1 / norm (the wet side). They maximise the (weighted) Poisson likelihood of O_y ~ c * P_y * g(z_y), with the level c profiled out (optim(), Nelder-Mead, from several starts), and ratio / norm, the upper level over the average, may not exceed 3 times the largest observed year total over the mean of the observed year totals, max(O_y) / mean(O_y) (a fit with no gain over a flat multiplier stores k = 0, ratio = 1). The stored list is list(variable, center, scale, shape, k, ratio, norm, bounds). With weights = "climate" each year counts fireSenseUtils::annualYearWeights() in the fit. "loglinear" and "equal" is the term as before, to the last bit.
